(B) The new `section Lp` in MaximalFunction.lean (ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_memLp, eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq, memLp_maximalFunction_toReal, maximalFunctionLp, coeFn_maximalFunctionLp, maximalFunctionLp_toLp, enorm_maximalFunctionLp_le). findings.evidence: roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/PDE/README.md:244-246 states target 8 as weak (1,1) + strong (p,p) + LDT. `grep -rn "Lebesgue differentiation\|ae_tendsto_average" code/TauCeti` returns nothing. `grep -rn "maximalFunction" code/TauCeti -l` returns only Marcinkiewicz.lean and MaximalFunction.lean, so nothing downstream consumes the bundled map.
findings.fix: Drop the Lp section from this PR. If it is wanted, resubmit it citing what consumes it (e.g. a concrete Lane B.10 or Lane E use), or advance target 8 itself by proving the Lebesgue differentiation theorem.
findings.issue: `maximalFunctionLp` and its supporting lemmas are new material with no proximate roadmap target. Lane B target 8 asks for the maximal function, weak (1,1), strong (p,p), and the Lebesgue differentiation theorem; the first three are already on `main` and LDT is not addressed here. A bundled nonlinear `Lp F p μ → Lp ℝ p μ` map is not named by the target and has no in-repo consumer.

summary: The PR bundles two independent units: an operator-level generalization of the already-merged Marcinkiewicz truncation argument (in scope as a refactor), and an unrelated new Lp-quotient maximal-function API that depends on none of it. The Lp half is also periphery around Lane B target 8, whose remaining named deliverable (the Lebesgue differentiation theorem) is untouched.
